question: Which of the following salts is used in black and white photography?
solution:
The correct answer is __**AgBr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **AgBr (Silver Bromide)** is a crucial compound used in the field of black and white photography.
 
• It is sensitive to light, which is fundamental in capturing photographic images.
 
• When exposed to light, AgBr decomposes to silver and bromine, creating a latent image that can be developed into a visible photograph.
 
• AgBr crystals are used in photographic films and papers, playing a significant role in the traditional photographic process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photographic Process**

 
 
• The photographic process involves capturing images by exposing a light-sensitive material to light.
 
• In black and white photography, silver halides like AgBr are commonly used due to their sensitivity to light.
 
• After exposure, the film is developed using chemical solutions that reduce the silver halide to metallic silver, creating a visible image.
 
• The developed film is then fixed to remove any unexposed silver halide, ensuring the image is permanent and not sensitive to light anymore.
 
 
 
• **Silver Halides**
 
 
• Silver halides are compounds of silver with halogens (chlorine, bromine, iodine).
 
• They are used in photographic materials due to their light-sensitive properties.
 
• Common silver halides used in photography include silver bromide (AgBr), silver chloride (AgCl), and silver iodide (AgI).
 
• These compounds form the basis of traditional photographic films and papers.
 
 
 
• **Latent Image**
 
 
• A latent image is an invisible image created on a photographic film or paper after exposure to light.
 
• It is formed by the reaction of light with silver halide crystals, creating a small amount of metallic silver.
 
• The latent image is later developed into a visible image through chemical processing.
 
• This process involves amplifying the small amount of metallic silver into a visible, larger amount that forms the photograph.
 
 
 
• **Photographic Development**
 
 
• Development is a chemical process that converts the latent image into a visible image.
 
• The developer solution reduces the exposed silver halide crystals to metallic silver, forming the image.
 
• After development, the film or paper is fixed to remove unexposed silver halide, stabilizing the image.
 
• Finally, the material is washed to remove any remaining chemicals, making the photograph permanent and light-stable.
